### SP-474 - Persistence of brainstorm.vote_added

**Identity.** The subject is `collaboration_run_id`, `vote_id`; `owner_operation_id`, `idempotency_key` and `event_id` follow SP-460's recipe with it. The `vote_id` is the identity.

**Admission checks, in order.** SP-460's common run checks; status `active` (`run_state_invalid`); the proposal has a `brainstorm.proposal_added` event (`unknown_proposal`); the voter's `attempt_id` was started for its slot (`unknown_attempt`) and is not a Wonderer attempt (`wonderer_cannot_vote`); it is the slot's current attempt and has no outcome other than `completed` (`attempt_not_current`); the `vote_id` has no event under an earlier epoch (`vote_already_added`). Tallies count a vote while its attempt stays the slot's current attempt with no outcome other than `completed`.

**Consumers and checkpoint.** `storage.collaboration_projector.v1@1.0.0` applies it to the vote row (collaboration_vote_projection.v1): adds the vote row; the proposal row (collaboration_proposal_projection.v1): updates support, oppose and abstain tallies from counted votes, and advances the scope partition's checkpoint in the same transaction (SP-460, SP-278 by name). Its readers are `storage.collaboration_reader.run_view.v1@1.0.0`, `storage.collaboration_reader.inspection.v1@1.0.0`.

**Producer and first receipt.** `CollaborationRuntime` calls `storage.collaboration_append.v1@1.0.0` from `CollaborationRuntime.record_vote(VoteCast)` after the owner commit that holds the prepared event, and adopts `storage.first_append_receipt.resolve.v2` for it (SP-460). A lost acknowledgement returns the original receipt and appends nothing new.

**Custody and retention.** The vote's reason and evidence are text and stay in the vote record; the event carries the position, confidence and constraint IDs only. Its records are kept as long as the chat named by `thread_id` exists, under `RP-CHAT-THREAD-LIFETIME@1.0.0` once its Storage landing records it; its projection rows use `RP-PROJECTION-3GEN@1.0.0`.

**Withdrawal.** While it is withdrawn new BrainStorm runs are refused; an active BrainStorm cannot record votes and never infers one. The writer is cut off first, then the checkpoint core is withdrawn and readers fenced, then a governed rebuild keeps every original event (SP-460).

**Prepared source for `brainstorm.vote_added`.** This family uses the registered `collaboration_prepared_source` key and canonical transaction of SP-460, its own `Plans/collaboration_prepared_sources.schema.json#/$defs/brainstorm_vote_added` project/application holder pair, and the exact typed owners `https://puppetmaster.local/schemas/collaborative_workflows/1.0.0/collaborative_workflows_contracts.schema.json#/$defs/BrainstormVote` (Project) and `https://puppetmaster.local/schemas/collaborative_workflows/1.0.0/collaborative_workflows_contracts.schema.json#/$defs/BrainstormVote` (application). The owner reference recipe is source_record_ref in SP-460; its physical key, actual Storage instance, captured write epoch, owner hash, full semantic body and original operation/event identities must all join. Coherent backup/restore carries this exact snapshot and its referenced originals; no sibling source substitutes and no append before this family's admission. Newly authored owner contract under DL-090; native source provenance, transaction and restore remain NOT_RUN.

### SP-475 - Persistence of brainstorm.plan_synthesized

**Identity.** The subject is `collaboration_run_id`; `owner_operation_id`, `idempotency_key` and `event_id` follow SP-460's recipe with it. The run alone is the subject: a run has one synthesis identity, matching "exactly one synthesized Deep Plan document" (section 8.1).

**Admission checks, in order.** SP-460's common run checks; status `active` (`run_state_invalid`); the run has no synthesis event under an earlier epoch (`already_synthesized`).

**Consumers and checkpoint.** `storage.collaboration_projector.v1@1.0.0` applies it to the run row (collaboration_run_projection.v1): the synthesized Plan identity and version, and advances the scope partition's checkpoint in the same transaction (SP-460, SP-278 by name). Its readers are `storage.collaboration_reader.run_view.v1@1.0.0`, `storage.collaboration_reader.completion.v1@1.0.0`, `storage.collaboration_reader.inspection.v1@1.0.0`.

**Producer and first receipt.** `CollaborationRuntime` calls `storage.collaboration_append.v1@1.0.0` from `CollaborationRuntime.record_synthesis(PlanCreated)` after the owner commit that holds the prepared event, and adopts `storage.first_append_receipt.resolve.v2` for it (SP-460). A second synthesis request resolves to the original Plan identity and event; no second Plan is requested.

**Custody and retention.** The Plan's text belongs to the Plan owner; dissent and alternatives are counted, never quoted. Its records are kept as long as the chat named by `thread_id` exists, under `RP-CHAT-THREAD-LIFETIME@1.0.0` once its Storage landing records it; its projection rows use `RP-PROJECTION-3GEN@1.0.0`.

**Withdrawal.** While it is withdrawn new BrainStorm runs are refused; an active BrainStorm cannot record its Plan and cannot complete. The writer is cut off first, then the checkpoint core is withdrawn and readers fenced, then a governed rebuild keeps every original event (SP-460).

**Prepared source for `brainstorm.plan_synthesized`.** This family uses the registered `collaboration_prepared_source` key and canonical transaction of SP-460, its own `Plans/collaboration_prepared_sources.schema.json#/$defs/brainstorm_plan_synthesized` project/application holder pair, and the exact typed owners `https://puppetmaster.local/schemas/collaborative_workflows/1.0.0/collaborative_workflows_contracts.schema.json#/$defs/CollaborativeRun` (Project) and `https://puppetmaster.local/schemas/application-workflows/1.0.0/contracts.schema.json#/$defs/CollaborationRunApplicationV1` (application). The owner reference recipe is source_record_ref in SP-460; its physical key, actual Storage instance, captured write epoch, owner hash, full semantic body and original operation/event identities must all join. Coherent backup/restore carries this exact snapshot and its referenced originals; no sibling source substitutes and no append before this family's admission. Newly authored owner contract under DL-090; native source provenance, transaction and restore remain NOT_RUN.

### SP-476 - Persistence of review.finding_added

**Identity.** The subject is `collaboration_run_id`, `finding_id`; `owner_operation_id`, `idempotency_key` and `event_id` follow SP-460's recipe with it. The `finding_id` is the identity; findings that share a `finding_key` stay distinct records.

**Admission checks, in order.** SP-460's common run checks (a payload naming a non-Review run fails `lineage_mismatch`); status `active` (`run_state_invalid`); `target_hashes` equal the run's frozen pack hashes from its `collaboration.started` (`target_hash_mismatch`); every originating reviewer is a roster slot (`slot_not_in_roster`); the `finding_id` has no event under an earlier epoch (`finding_already_added`).

**Consumers and checkpoint.** `storage.collaboration_projector.v1@1.0.0` applies it to the finding row (collaboration_finding_projection.v1): adds the finding row, undisposed, and advances the scope partition's checkpoint in the same transaction (SP-460, SP-278 by name). Its readers are `storage.collaboration_reader.run_view.v1@1.0.0`, `storage.collaboration_reader.review_followon.v1@1.0.0`, `storage.collaboration_reader.inspection.v1@1.0.0`.

**Producer and first receipt.** `CollaborationRuntime` calls `storage.collaboration_append.v1@1.0.0` from `CollaborationRuntime.release_finding(FindingNormalized)` after the owner commit that holds the prepared event, and adopts `storage.first_append_receipt.resolve.v2` for it (SP-460). A lost acknowledgement returns the original receipt and appends nothing new.

**Custody and retention.** Text protection (DL-090). The event carries no finding text: no claim, category, evidence, dissent or proposed remediation. That text stays in the finding record, which finding_record_ref names. Deleting the chat deletes the event under the chat-lifetime policy; the record and its text follow the same chat lifetime, holds and deletion deadlines under E-CARDS-1 1c A. Readers disclose a finding only after normalization releases it (CWR-013). Its records are kept as long as the chat named by `thread_id` exists, under `RP-CHAT-THREAD-LIFETIME@1.0.0` once its Storage landing records it; its projection rows use `RP-PROJECTION-3GEN@1.0.0`.

**Withdrawal.** While it is withdrawn new Review runs are refused; an active Review cannot normalize findings and cannot finalize. The writer is cut off first, then the checkpoint core is withdrawn and readers fenced, then a governed rebuild keeps every original event (SP-460).

**Prepared source for `review.finding_added`.** This family uses the registered `collaboration_prepared_source` key and canonical transaction of SP-460, its own `Plans/collaboration_prepared_sources.schema.json#/$defs/review_finding_added` project/application holder pair, and the exact typed owners `https://puppetmaster.local/schemas/collaborative_workflows/1.0.0/collaborative_workflows_contracts.schema.json#/$defs/ReviewFinding` (Project) and `https://puppetmaster.local/schemas/collaborative_workflows/1.0.0/collaborative_workflows_contracts.schema.json#/$defs/ReviewFinding` (application). The owner reference recipe is source_record_ref in SP-460; its physical key, actual Storage instance, captured write epoch, owner hash, full semantic body and original operation/event identities must all join. Coherent backup/restore carries this exact snapshot and its referenced originals; no sibling source substitutes and no append before this family's admission. Newly authored owner contract under DL-090; native source provenance, transaction and restore remain NOT_RUN.

### SP-477 - Persistence of review.finding_dispositioned

**Identity.** The subject is `collaboration_run_id`, `finding_id`; `owner_operation_id`, `idempotency_key` and `event_id` follow SP-460's recipe with it. The `finding_id` is the identity: one final disposition per finding.

**Admission checks, in order.** SP-460's common run checks; status `active` (`run_state_invalid`); the finding has a `review.finding_added` event (`unknown_finding`) and no disposition (`already_dispositioned`); `target_hashes` equal the finding's (`target_hash_mismatch`).

**Consumers and checkpoint.** `storage.collaboration_projector.v1@1.0.0` applies it to the finding row (collaboration_finding_projection.v1): the final disposition, confidence and dissent count, and advances the scope partition's checkpoint in the same transaction (SP-460, SP-278 by name). Its readers are `storage.collaboration_reader.run_view.v1@1.0.0`, `storage.collaboration_reader.review_followon.v1@1.0.0`, `storage.collaboration_reader.inspection.v1@1.0.0`.

**Producer and first receipt.** `CollaborationRuntime` calls `storage.collaboration_append.v1@1.0.0` from `CollaborationRuntime.record_adjudication(FindingAdjudicated)` after the owner commit that holds the prepared event, and adopts `storage.first_append_receipt.resolve.v2` for it (SP-460). A lost acknowledgement returns the original receipt and appends nothing new.

**Custody and retention.** Text protection (DL-090). Dissent and the adjudication's reasoning are text and stay in the finding record; the event carries counts, the closed disposition and refs only. Its deletion follows the chat, and the record and its text follow the chat lifetime, holds and deletion deadlines under E-CARDS-1 1c A. Its records are kept as long as the chat named by `thread_id` exists, under `RP-CHAT-THREAD-LIFETIME@1.0.0` once its Storage landing records it; its projection rows use `RP-PROJECTION-3GEN@1.0.0`.

**Withdrawal.** While it is withdrawn new Review runs are refused; an active Review cannot record dispositions and cannot finalize. The writer is cut off first, then the checkpoint core is withdrawn and readers fenced, then a governed rebuild keeps every original event (SP-460).

**Prepared source for `review.finding_dispositioned`.** This family uses the registered `collaboration_prepared_source` key and canonical transaction of SP-460, its own `Plans/collaboration_prepared_sources.schema.json#/$defs/review_finding_dispositioned` project/application holder pair, and the exact typed owners `https://puppetmaster.local/schemas/collaborative_workflows/1.0.0/collaborative_workflows_contracts.schema.json#/$defs/ReviewFinding` (Project) and `https://puppetmaster.local/schemas/collaborative_workflows/1.0.0/collaborative_workflows_contracts.schema.json#/$defs/ReviewFinding` (application). The owner reference recipe is source_record_ref in SP-460; its physical key, actual Storage instance, captured write epoch, owner hash, full semantic body and original operation/event identities must all join. Coherent backup/restore carries this exact snapshot and its referenced originals; no sibling source substitutes and no append before this family's admission. Newly authored owner contract under DL-090; native source provenance, transaction and restore remain NOT_RUN.

### SP-478 - Persistence of review.artifact_finalized

**Identity.** The subject is `collaboration_run_id`; `owner_operation_id`, `idempotency_key` and `event_id` follow SP-460's recipe with it. The run alone is the subject: a Review run finalizes one artifact; Run Another Review is a new run.

**Admission checks, in order.** SP-460's common run checks; status `active` (`run_state_invalid`); no finalization exists (`already_finalized`); every added finding has a disposition (`findings_not_dispositioned`); the `artifact_version_ref` has a `collaboration.artifact_added` event in the run (`artifact_not_added`); `target_hashes` equal the run's (`target_hash_mismatch`); fewer completed than requested reviewers needs `partial_coverage_accepted` and a recorded waiver in the run (`partial_not_accepted`); `stale_target_accepted` needs a recorded reconfigure with `accept_stale_target` (`stale_not_accepted`).

**Consumers and checkpoint.** `storage.collaboration_projector.v1@1.0.0` applies it to the run row (collaboration_run_projection.v1): the finalized Review artifact, coverage and staleness, and advances the scope partition's checkpoint in the same transaction (SP-460, SP-278 by name). Its readers are `storage.collaboration_reader.run_view.v1@1.0.0`, `storage.collaboration_reader.completion.v1@1.0.0`, `storage.collaboration_reader.review_followon.v1@1.0.0`, `storage.collaboration_reader.inspection.v1@1.0.0`.

**Producer and first receipt.** `CollaborationRuntime` calls `storage.collaboration_append.v1@1.0.0` from `CollaborationRuntime.finalize_review(ReviewArtifactFinalized)` after the owner commit that holds the prepared event, and adopts `storage.first_append_receipt.resolve.v2` for it (SP-460). A retry resolves to the original finalization; the thread summary links the same version.

**Custody and retention.** The artifact's text stays with the artifact owner; the event carries refs, hashes, counts and flags only. Its records are kept as long as the chat named by `thread_id` exists, under `RP-CHAT-THREAD-LIFETIME@1.0.0` once its Storage landing records it; its projection rows use `RP-PROJECTION-3GEN@1.0.0`.

**Withdrawal.** While it is withdrawn new Review runs are refused; an active Review cannot finalize and cannot complete. The writer is cut off first, then the checkpoint core is withdrawn and readers fenced, then a governed rebuild keeps every original event (SP-460).

**Prepared source for `review.artifact_finalized`.** This family uses the registered `collaboration_prepared_source` key and canonical transaction of SP-460, its own `Plans/collaboration_prepared_sources.schema.json#/$defs/review_artifact_finalized` project/application holder pair, and the exact typed owners `https://puppetmaster.local/schemas/collaborative_workflows/1.0.0/collaborative_workflows_contracts.schema.json#/$defs/CollaborativeRun` (Project) and `https://puppetmaster.local/schemas/application-workflows/1.0.0/contracts.schema.json#/$defs/CollaborationRunApplicationV1` (application). The owner reference recipe is source_record_ref in SP-460; its physical key, actual Storage instance, captured write epoch, owner hash, full semantic body and original operation/event identities must all join. Coherent backup/restore carries this exact snapshot and its referenced originals; no sibling source substitutes and no append before this family's admission. Newly authored owner contract under DL-090; native source provenance, transaction and restore remain NOT_RUN.

### SP-580 - approval.requested prepared event contract

```yaml
plan_unit_id: SP-580
unit_type: schema_contract
status: accepted
owner_doc: Plans/storage-plan.md
canonical_text: |-
  Newly authored owner contract under DL-045 for approval.requested only. Producer HITLBlockedEpisodeOwner.requested calls storage.dt.approval_requested.append.v1@1.0.0. Validate exact family/version and actual source, scope, permissions and transition before body/intent commit; record the immutable source/result reference durably before append. Adopt SP-286 and CV-339 storage.first_append_receipt.resolve.v2 by name, including full-value custody, and SP-336/SP-347 group durability. First AppendReceipt follows committed group durability; approval/receipt barriers require full flush. Publish terminal result, progression or queue release only after the original receipt resolves. Uncertain append fences later subject work until resolution; missing receipt never authorizes a fresh identity or repeated external effect. Replay retrieves original source/result and never dispatches a tool, issues approval, recreates/deletes a worktree, enqueues work, charges usage or sends a notification. For approval.requested, allocate the original source operation identity before any effect. Its idempotency_key is 'dt:' plus lowercase SHA-256 of RFC 8785 JSON [event_type, scope_partition, run_id, node_id, blocked_sequence, approval_scope_key], preserving those exact source values. event_id is 'evt_dt_' plus SHA-256 of UTF-8 idempotency_key. Use dedupe_by_idempotency_key and the complete CV-EventRecord producer_semantic_digest; same identity/different semantic digest refuses idempotency_conflict. Retries retain occurred_at_utc and every source/envelope field. The operating consumer storage.dt.approval_requested.reader.v1@1.0.0 serves HITL resolver, runtime blocked controls and inspection; it directly filters verified EventRecord index reads for this exact family, not an invented second domain database. It explicitly adopts SP-278 and DL-076's nine-field durable token, never persisted redb_snapshot_id. Checkpoint key projector.checkpoint.dt.approval_requested:{storage_instance_id}:{scope_partition} stores Plans/dt_event_contracts.schema.json#/$defs/approval_requested_checkpoint. The inclusive examined_through_sequence_id advances over every examined source row, including nonmatching rows; last_applied_event_id is the last matching row or null. Validate storage instance, partition, token generation/frontier/coverage/source selection and exact admitted family/version before publication. Process a prefix and publish the cursor/token/filter completeness atomically under exact previous-value CAS and a fenced writer lease; losing CAS publishes nothing. Empty source is proven by the source token, never guessed from no matches. Readers require current/healthy/filter_complete coverage for their requested prefix and recheck current permission, tombstones, source selection and withdrawal before returning any record. Rebuild from verified retained source with recovery holds, never from checkpoint alone; source gaps return unavailable, never silently skip them. Derived checkpoint retention is RP-PROJECTION-3GEN with source holds and at most three same-key generations. Canonical seglog originals and referenced bodies remain under mandatory coherent backup/restore, source access and deletion checks; opaque refs grant no access. Keep credentials, tool arguments, raw output and private file contents out of this payload; refs are opaque permission-checked locators, bounded reasons/previews are redacted before persistence. Backup restores original source, dedupe/receipt custody and references coherently or fences mutation; checkpoints rebuild, and an older restore never revives a resolved approval or deleted worktree. Unknown version refuses current mutation and disclosure until a validating reader/upgrader is installed; legacy aliases normalize before persistence only with original source proof, never by replay side effects. Withdrawal first cuts off this family's append admission, then fences its consumer/readers and marks checkpoint withdrawn with a fixed timestamp. No advance or ordinary read follows; governed compatible rebuild and revalidated source/admission are required to resume. No zero-cursor reset, sibling substitution or history rewrite. retention_policy_ref = RP-AUTHORITY-INDEFINITE. Case L-3 directly names Approval: indefinite, no count eviction, fail closed under pressure. Holds, original anchors and dependency checks are unchanged; retries never reset the retention anchor. Checks and positive/negative fixtures: python3 scripts/pm-dt-event-contracts.py; ATS-290. Native execution remains NOT_RUN. No registry append, admission, owner decision or seal follows.
  For approval.requested alone, the newly authored original-source custody is dt_approval_requested_source at storage/event-sources/dt/approval_requested/{event_id}/{stage}.json, strict Plans/dt_event_contracts.schema.json#/$defs/approval_requested_source; no sibling source is accepted. The codec is pm.dt.source.json.v1 canonical UTF-8 JSON without BOM/newline, maximum 1048576 bytes per stage; reject duplicate keys, nonfinite numbers, malformed Unicode, unknown fields and unsupported version. SHA-256 binds exact bytes; file paths are derived from the validated event_id and literal stage under this Storage instance, never caller paths. HITLBlockedEpisodeOwner.requested owns preparation and authenticates HITLBlockedEpisodeOwner.requested.resolve_original against the actual original human-in-the-loop.md owner_ref/revision, not the caller's witness or today's reconstructed configuration. Install the exact source schema/codec and append admission via StorageMigrationCoordinator, then validate current family admission, scope, actor and all family predicates before preparing or performing work. Publish prepared.json once under the subject owner lock using SP-131 same-directory temp/fsync/no-overwrite promotion and synchronized parent entries; allocate the original identity first. A byte-identical existing stage is reused; different bytes fence the subject. The owner's existing operation commits its result with this source identity in its original outcome; the resolver proves that join against the actual owner transaction/receipt before completed.json is durably promoted. This is a recoverable prepare/outcome handshake, not an atomic commit across an external tool or Git and Storage. A crash after prepare but before provable outcome remains fenced; query the original owner operation by this exact allocated identity. If it cannot prove original outcome, return unavailable and do not repeat any effect. completed.json is immutable, links prepared_sha256, carries the exact redacted closed payload and frozen envelope_context, and names the immutable owner_outcome_ref. Only then append the exact EventRecord; SP-286/CV-339 full-value v2 resolves the first eleven-field receipt, including its original seal-time timestamp. Source and completed payload/identity/envelope joins and current owner permissions/deletion are revalidated under the final owner lock after every helper. For this family require a barrier-class full flush through original outcome/source files, packs, segment commit frame and canonical receipt before terminal publication or authorizing dependent work. This is a stronger event-specific barrier within SP-336/SP-347, not a change to ordinary receipt loss. Lost acknowledgement returns the original full value and receipt; no fabricated replacement time/result/identity. Source stages, original owner outcomes, referenced bodies and full-value receipt custody form one mandatory coherent backup closure. An older restore missing any delivered member fences retry/mutation and discloses unavailable; no restore manufactures or replays an external result. Original source retention is the event's unchanged RP-AUTHORITY-INDEFINITE dependency, including all owner holds/backups; no new expiry/count/deletion choice. A PENDING_RETENTION_DECISION source or event cannot be admitted. Source bytes are bounded redacted metadata and permission-checked original refs, never raw config/tool output/credentials. The exact new source schema and resolver are technical custody bindings only; no new command, feature or user-visible frequency is selected.
  For approval.requested alone, its SP-278/DL-076 checkpoint uses null examined_through_sequence_id and null last_applied_event_id for a proven empty prefix; sequence zero is not a fabricated cursor. A nonempty prefix stores the final globally examined sequence, including nonmatching events. The nine-field durable token must equal the actual current generic-index capture (storage instance, root/node/dataset, generation anchor, frontier revision/hash and source_selection); reacquire the live redb snapshot without persisting its id. Capture complete global source coverage, source-frame verification and exact filter/version before evaluating any matching row. The source-verified rows are authoritative; a matching witness hash alone is insufficient. Under the source/maintenance fence and the exact consumer writer lease, recheck the entire old checkpoint value, current token, admission/installed-reader, permissions, tombstones and withdrawal; one redb transaction CASes the entire checkpoint. Failed CAS, changed frontier/source, missing retained prefix, future source version or any failed final guard publishes nothing and returns unavailable. Rows from any Project/application partition remain part of global examined coverage even when filtered out. Empty global source and a nonempty prefix with zero family matches are separate cases. Withdraw first cuts off new append admission under coordinator exclusion; drain admitted receipts, fence reader CAS and fix withdrawn_at_utc once. A withdrawn checkpoint cannot advance or disclose; reinstallation requires fresh governed source verification/rebuild, never zero reset. Rebuild reads retained canonical source and original source/receipt closures under recovery holds; at most three same-key generations, no source eviction from checkpoint pressure. Readers only inspect; recovery never performs a tool, approval, enqueue, notification, Settings or worktree action.
  For approval.requested alone, source codec pm.dt.source.json.v1 writes null/booleans as JSON literals, integers in exact shortest signed decimal (nonnegative source counters retain u64 without float conversion), finite fractional numbers as exact plain decimals with trailing fractional zeroes removed (no exponent and negative zero becomes zero), UTF-8 strings with JSON quote/backslash/control escaping and no Unicode normalization, arrays in order, and closed-object keys ordered by strict UTF-8 bytes. Duplicate keys, malformed Unicode, BOM, whitespace outside strings and nonfinite numbers are refused. Source decoder uses exact decimal parsing, not IEEE-754 conversion; a complete canonical-byte reencode must equal the input. This is a newly authored source-file codec, not a change to EventRecord's RFC 8785 semantic digest. For the identity preimage only, every unsigned integer subject is its shortest unsigned decimal string; thus all elements of the RFC 8785 array are strings. scope_partition is the existing Storage app or project~base64url(UTF-8 actual project_id without padding), never literal caller concatenation.
  For approval.requested, boolean authority/context flags are exact booleans before their value is evaluated. Numeric and boolean fields are validated against their declared owner types before joins; typed canonical comparisons distinguish booleans from numbers. A prior checkpoint must validate before CAS/state comparisons. Prefix rows must be objects with owner-valid unsigned integer sequence ids and nonempty string event type, event id and scope partition before filtering. This type-safety rule changes no numeric spelling, integer range, physical bytes or retained-history recipe.
  For approval.requested alone, the explicit lifecycle transition is blocked -> requested: request action set is captured; no grant or tool execution. prepared.before contains only original prerequisites known before the owner operation; completed.owner_result contains the closed authentic original outcome fields, which cannot be guessed at prepare time. The original owner commits those fields under the preallocated subject identity; payload outcome fields must equal that result. A completed source is accepted only with the exact prepare digest, original owner result and complete captured joins. No immutable prepared record is overwritten with a later outcome. Duplicate delivery returns the complete original receipt/value; invalid predecessors or changed prerequisites refuse without a new append or dependent publication. The named resolve_original method takes exactly storage_instance_id, scope_partition, event_id, idempotency_key, owner_ref and owner_revision; it returns exactly unavailable(reason_code) or original(prepared source, completed source, original full EventRecord, original eleven-field AppendReceipt or null before issuance). These records use this family's exact schemas and immutable files; the method authenticates actual owner transactions/files/permissions, never a caller assertion. Before issuance it may finalize from a provable original outcome and append only the frozen original; a missing or uncertain owner result remains unavailable/fenced.
  For approval.requested alone, the materialized checkpoint verified_prefix adapter binds the complete nine-field token, exact globally examined row-set digest/count/range and filter result; a transplanted row-set or token is unavailable. This synthetic adapter is an explicit native-authentication assumption, not a claim that fixture booleans authenticate Storage frames. The source codec byte vectors, exact source/owner_result separation, application server/operation/codec negatives where applicable, independent lifecycle transitions, pending/known retention gates and held-generation capacity cases are executable static oracles in scripts/pm-dt-event-contracts.py. Each recovery/checkpoint fixture is also a concrete native crash/race obligation; original owner transaction, fsync, wire, permissions and redb CAS remain NOT_RUN.
  For approval.requested alone, the ordinary canonical append/read path adopts Case L-2, SP-026 and SP-236 SeglogFrameV2 without a family-specific wire decoder or new header. SP-337 owns the 16 KiB inline limit and BLAKE3 payload-pack addressing; a separately governed or larger payload is resolved through the actual permission-checked pack reader before schema/join validation. A pack body and its index are durable before the referencing group receipt; a missing, changed, unverified or deleted pack body is unavailable, never an empty successful result. The full-value receipt preserves the actual inline/ref producer fields unchanged; decoding the body never rewrites its original semantic digest.
```

**bundle.selection_forward_blocked domain projection binding (newly authored owner contract).** Exact domain projector `projector.chat.bundle_selection_forward_blocked@1.0.0` 1.0.0 and operating consumer `reader.chat.bundle_selection_forward_blocked@1.0.0` explicitly adopt SP-278 and the same verified full-index source path. The family's separate checkpoint is `projector.checkpoint.dch.bundle_selection_forward_blocked.v1:{storage_instance_id}:{scope_partition}`, stored family `dch_bundle_selection_forward_blocked_checkpoint`, closed schema `Plans/dch_event_payloads/dch_bundle_selection_forward_blocked_checkpoint.schema.json#`, schema_id `pm.storage_value.dch_bundle_selection_forward_blocked_checkpoint.v1` 1.0.0. The nine-field durable token is copied exactly from SP-278/DL-076 without redb_snapshot_id. Consumer/projector versions are the suffixes in their stored constant IDs; no version is inferred from the payload. `last_sequence_id` and `last_event_id` identify the last applied exact-family EventRecord; `source_token` identifies complete inspected source coverage including nonmatching events. Publication identity is fresh entropy for a new shadow generation and frozen on retries; revision increments exactly once on successful CAS. The key joins storage_instance_id and scope_partition exactly. Application partition app is also bound to its source token's Server/instance and the event's Computer/thread, never to every null Project. The projector processes this family's records in verified source sequence order and performs only the transition of ACD-610. For `chat.message`, resolve and authorize its canonical typed message and build SP-338 pages and Tantivy fields once keyed by (thread_id,message_id); never reopen a deleted/superseded message. For thread lifecycle, take current lifecycle from the canonical revision and tombstone rather than treating an old historical event as current. Worktree fields update only the existing owner-defined binding/reverse/worktree projections, with old/new identity checks; no git effect is replayed. Selection events attach only existing authorized outcome/provenance refs to audit/pending-chip status; never create a chip or repeat a send during replay. Failure events retain actual original error evidence and cannot imply a successful outcome.

For this exact family, publish projection mutation and checkpoint revision together in one redb transaction with predecessor revision/publication_id CAS. Where the target is Tantivy or the SP-338 page payload store, first durably stage and read back an immutable shadow commit, put its exact reference in projection_refs, then CAS-publish the pointer and checkpoint together. Readers serve only targets named by the current checkpoint's refs and same publication_id; old/partial targets never become visible by newest-file inference. Existing canonical thread/worktree state is not rewritten by a derived rebuild. Rebuild any shared target from all its admitted family sources in global source order into one shadow, never by replaying a whole bound family after an unbound family. A required unadmitted counterpart fences that target, not an inferred admission. Re-read canonical state/tombstones and current grants before publication. On source-generation change or failed CAS, discard unpublished target or retry from the unchanged verified prefix; never reuse a stale token. Missing or malformed derived bytes enter Q-DERIVED and governed rebuild, not source repair. Source loss requires canonical backup recovery.

The checkpoint is MessagePack canonical, max 16 KiB under SP-340; oversized values use existing SP-337 reference storage, never an exemption. The closed history array stores at most two full prior checkpoint generations with first retired_at_utc and state retired; current fields name the selected generation. Reserve staged slots through the existing maintenance intent before source staging; a staged candidate counts against three even before it is visible in history. Retain at most three publication generations per exact key under RP-PROJECTION-3GEN@1.0.0; retirement starts at first committed replacement, retries do not reset it, 604800 seconds for eligible retired generations only, with holds/current/staged/live-ref protection. Reserve the slot first or disclose rebuild unavailability. Source events keep PENDING_RETENTION_DECISION; the checkpoint gives no source keepalive. Backup restores canonical source/custody/tombstones first; derived target/checkpoint is rebuilt and validated against the current full-index token before read. Withdrawal fences this projector and its domain readers in addition to the passive reader, sets checkpoint state withdrawn by CAS, and refuses all ordinary advances. Retained historical lookup uses original schema and current access checks; successor publication requires a separately versioned, complete shadow rebuild. Unsupported versions are unavailable, never rewritten in place.

Adopt SP-337 for this exact event body. The logical body remains the selected closed Project/application payload edition, with its existing field and array bounds unchanged. Encode that complete body as SP-236 canonical MessagePack (recursive exact UTF-8 map-key order and shortest encodings); measure encoded bytes, not JSON characters or the envelope. At most 16384 bytes may be inline with payload_ref=null. An oversized inline body is refused before append. Larger or separately governed bodies use payload={} and the newly authored string binding `payload:v1:{lowercase_blake3_64}:{decimal_byte_size}:application/msgpack` in EventRecord.payload_ref, with canonical unsigned decimal size, selecting the existing payload-pack index key `payload:v1:{lowercase_blake3_64}`. The reference commits to the BLAKE3 of the exact complete encoded body, exact byte size and media type application/msgpack. Resolve and decode that original body, validate its exact schema/edition and every scope/identity/actor/time join as for inline bodies; a reference is never an empty semantic body. Require actual original Storage instance, Server/scope/Computer/thread custody, current authorization/deletion/hold access checks, durable exact pack bytes and index entry and verified readback before the referencing append can be acknowledged or its first receipt/result published. Missing, changed, unauthorized, deleted, wrong-store or unreadable body/index evidence refuses publication; no base64 body, truncated body, alternate-source reconstruction or rerun is allowed. Pack durability, reference counts, holds, backups and deletion deadlines remain SP-337; this binding grants no new retention exemption.

Checkpoint acceptance compares original source facts independently of the candidate: the outer storage_instance_id, durable-token storage_instance_id, source_selection storage_instance_id and actual source/root instance must be identical. Resolve the token checkpoint_key in the actual full-index root, its uniquely current generation JSON Pointer checkpoint_ref and exact same-instance event_record_index.v2@generation dataset. Require exact generation anchor, current frontier revision/digest and all source_selection fields against current synchronized source, including nonmatching same-generation appends; a shape-valid stale token cannot publish. The domain checkpoint key binds this instance and exact scope_partition. last_event_id/last_sequence_id join the actual exact-family EventRecord and its full-index row and source-value commitment; actual source Computer/thread/scope also join the published projection. Publication_id, revision, projection_refs and the full durable source token match the actual staged/read-back publication selected by the atomic checkpoint/pointer CAS. Independent source, token, selection, key/ref, event, dataset, publication and current-frontier mismatches refuse publication. Static fixture adapters model these joins; they do not prove native full-index coverage, redb transactions, CRC, source locks or durability.

For bundle.selection_forward_blocked, the complete encoded checkpoint includes every retained history entry and projection reference. Measure that entire SP-236 value at the 16384-byte SP-340 boundary: 16384 bytes may be inline, 16385 bytes may not. A larger logical checkpoint keeps the same closed schema and bounds and uses SP-337; measure the stored reference/pointer too. Resolve the exact complete bytes through their BLAKE3/size/media-type reference and same-instance, exact-key/scope/family payload-pack index, with current authorization/deletion/hold access, durable bytes/index and verified readback before checkpoint publication. Externalizing the event body does not externalize this checkpoint. Every Storage-assigned identity and metadata field is checked against the original Storage record for the actual instance; no fixture/default instance supplies authority. Checkpoint source lookup resolves inline or referenced originals, validates the supported original envelope and Project/application payload edition, verifies their exact original source commitment and current access/withdrawal status, and then joins their source facts. Retained compatibility-reader originals, including projector_replay_only, remain readable after later live-state changes; only a new append/retry uses the current-writer policy. Unsupported, withdrawn, forged or foreign originals cannot publish. Newly written integer and boolean slots require their exact types before comparison or arithmetic; string numbers/booleans, null, arrays and nested objects confer no numeric or access authority. Current physical commitment/reference encoding canonicalizes integral numeric aliases and signed zero to the same shortest integer bytes; retained bytes retain their protected original recipe below. These are refinements of this family's existing SP-236/SP-278/SP-337/SP-340 contract, not a new retention or product decision.

Before any source resolution or identity hashing, validate every Storage-instance context against Storage's own UUID descriptor in Plans/event_record_index_checkpoint.schema.json, including exact primitive type and UUID format. Empty, malformed, overlong, newline-suffixed and non-string instances refuse even when dependent IDs, keys and source commitments agree. Compare candidate, token, source-selection, payload-pack and index context against the independently read actual Storage record; a caller context, default instance or coherent forged context supplies no authority. Verify Storage-assigned sequence and timestamp fields against that exact original record commitment before reading. A retained original remains governed by its supported edition and current custody, not later lifecycle state.

For new writes and current identity/idempotency inputs, this family selects strict-v4 exact integer types with the owner-declared domain of each field. Storage sequence_id and its last_sequence_id copies, frontier_revision, selected_segment_generation, manifest_generation, recovery_epoch and pack byte_size retain exact uint64 values 0 through 18446744073709551615; no 2^53 ceiling applies to Storage metadata. Publication revision and logical payload integers retain their existing owner minima and maxima, with no invented DCH safe-integer cap. Declared integer slots reject runtime float/string/bool/null/array/object substitutes except explicitly nullable slots. Storage metadata is excluded from the producer-semantic projection as already specified. The producer route is the CV-1100 qualified RFC 8785 encoding of the unchanged CV-317 producer projection (shared producer_semantic_bytes/producer_semantic_digest); an unsupported exact producer input is a structured route refusal, without narrowing its logical owner domain, rounding or stringification. Physical bytes follow SP-236 through the shared SP-1100 codec (storage_value_bytes, EVENT_VALUE profile): float type, minimal exact float width and signed zero are preserved, so a lexical alias never shares an integer's bytes, and the exact integer slots refuse every alias; invalid JSON 01 refuses under the CV-1100 current parser. Retained-recipe dispatch composes the shared SP-1101 RetainedDispatcher and timestamps use the shared CV-1101 check, as the retained-original and format paragraphs state. Test Storage write/retry inputs at 2^53, 2^60 and uint64 maximum, and refuse overflow, negative and wrong-type metadata independently.

Retained and compatibility originals use the schema, numeric domain, runtime type policy, format validator and physical encoder in force when written. The single selector record_number_rule() owns this dispatch on passive history, SP-337 materialization/reference verification, full-index source/checkpoint validation, checkpoint physical storage, saved-original retry comparison and terminal retained-start lookup. New/current inputs select strict-v4. For retained sources, independently read protected Storage write-receipt provenance binds actual storage_instance_id, exact original source-value SHA-256 and recipe_id; it is committed with the original write and survives restore with that source. Candidate fields, caller version/recipe flags, mutable live state and payload content cannot select or enroll an earlier recipe. Verify any claim against that independently authenticated provenance, then verify the exact original bytes with the selected recipe. Missing earlier provenance is unavailable under that earlier recipe, never a guessed downgrade: an original of a Store outside the sealed write custody refuses as unavailable and a receipt naming a recipe with no installed frozen verifier refuses as unsupported, with no fallback to another recipe; within a custody Store an original without a legacy receipt was written by the current strict-v4 writer. Each retained read composes the shared SP-1101 RetainedDispatcher once: one owner selection, no caller override and no current-then-legacy probing, and the installed frozen verifier of that exact recipe tuple (pinned to the recipe's recorded original schema hashes) checks the original. Preserve raw-v1 (d36809af original MessagePack numeric types), normalized-v2 (a785466d normalized integral floats with the original uncapped integer domain), and strict-v3 (c21fa62e safe integers; its original checker skipped date-time and URI formats); Plans/dch_retained_recipes.json pins their exact original schemas and source revisions. A skipped format check never authenticates invalid history (CV-1101, SP-1101): frozen validators apply the shared date-time predicate and CV-253 to the recipe's pinned original resources, so a retained timestamp CV-1101 refuses is owner-invalid and refuses, while owner-valid lowercase, leap-second and long-fraction history stays readable with its exact spelling; the skipped URI check is preserved. Never re-encode raw-v1 bytes under a later normalization to verify their commitment. Plans/dch_write_recipe_receipts.json is an independent synthetic Storage receipt adapter, not native authentication evidence. Every earlier-valid retained numeric or format record stays readable with current authorization, deletion/hold access, withdrawal and actual-source identity checks. A forged source or recipe selection still refuses. Current derived checkpoints may copy an old event sequence into their exact new integer representation; the original retained event/index sequence and commitment remain unchanged. A retry verifies its saved original through the same historical schema/byte/custody reader before comparison; its incoming input stays strict-v4, and a replay-only compatibility original still cannot authorize a current append or retry. Different earlier semantic values conflict without sending an out-of-current-domain original through the current RFC 8785 encoder. A retained checkpoint, including its history and physical payload pack, uses its own original write provenance separately from its referenced event.

The strict-v4 format validators are mandatory and installed explicitly, never through optional jsonschema plugins. Timestamps adopt the shared CV-1101 check: every current and frozen DCH validator is pm_event_datetime.datetime_validator over the complete outer schema, so the registered RFC 3339 predicate runs through the validator. occurred_at_utc keeps the EventRecord profile (T or t, Z/z or a signed offset, any fraction length, year 0000 and legitimate offset-adjusted leap seconds); observed_at_utc and persisted_at_utc keep CV-253's storage_utc_z profile through the inventory-classified envelope; the family ts and populated checkpoint retired_at_utc take the same predicate with their unchanged owner-schema terminal uppercase-Z pattern. A missing zone, space or wrong separator, invalid calendar field, hour 24, minute 60, false leap second, empty fraction and trailing LF refuse. Timestamp strings are never rewritten and are compared only as exact strings; no DCH-local timestamp grammar remains. PR URLs where declared fully match RFC 3986 HTTPS syntax, including valid percent escapes, reg-name or bracketed IPv6/IPvFuture host, numeric port and path/query/fragment grammar. Malformed brackets/hosts/escapes and whitespace refuse. No PR-host allowlist or new provider behavior is introduced. UUID contexts keep Storage's enforced descriptor. Both payload editions, all three EventRecord timestamps and populated checkpoint retirement times have isolated format negatives; applicable PR payloads cover every malformed URL form.

Explicitly adopt SP-278 including DL-076 nine-field durable read token and current full-index generation/frontier validation; no persisted redb_snapshot_id. Storage metadata is excluded from the producer-semantic projection as already specified. The producer route is the CV-1100 qualified RFC 8785 encoding of the unchanged CV-317 producer projection (shared producer_semantic_bytes/producer_semantic_digest); an unsupported exact producer input is a structured route refusal, without narrowing its logical owner domain, rounding or stringification. Physical bytes follow SP-236 through the shared SP-1100 codec (storage_value_bytes, EVENT_VALUE profile): float type, minimal exact float width and signed zero are preserved, so a lexical alias never shares an integer's bytes, and the exact integer slots refuse every alias; invalid JSON 01 refuses under the CV-1100 current parser. Retained-recipe dispatch composes the shared SP-1101 RetainedDispatcher and timestamps use the shared CV-1101 check, as the retained-original and format paragraphs state. Test Storage write/retry inputs at 2^53, 2^60 and uint64 maximum, and refuse overflow, negative and wrong-type metadata independently.

```yaml
Retained and compatibility originals use the schema, numeric domain, runtime type policy, format validator and physical encoder in force when written. The single selector record_number_rule() owns this dispatch on passive history, SP-337 materialization/reference verification, full-index source/checkpoint validation, checkpoint physical storage, saved-original retry comparison and terminal retained-start lookup. New/current inputs select strict-v4. For retained sources, independently read protected Storage write-receipt provenance binds actual storage_instance_id, exact original source-value SHA-256 and recipe_id; it is committed with the original write and survives restore with that source. Candidate fields, caller version/recipe flags, mutable live state and payload content cannot select or enroll an earlier recipe. Verify any claim against that independently authenticated provenance, then verify the exact original bytes with the selected recipe. Missing earlier provenance is unavailable under that earlier recipe, never a guessed downgrade: an original of a Store outside the sealed write custody refuses as unavailable and a receipt naming a recipe with no installed frozen verifier refuses as unsupported, with no fallback to another recipe; within a custody Store an original without a legacy receipt was written by the current strict-v4 writer. Each retained read composes the shared SP-1101 RetainedDispatcher once: one owner selection, no caller override and no current-then-legacy probing, and the installed frozen verifier of that exact recipe tuple (pinned to the recipe's recorded original schema hashes) checks the original. Preserve raw-v1 (d36809af original MessagePack numeric types), normalized-v2 (a785466d normalized integral floats with the original uncapped integer domain), and strict-v3 (c21fa62e safe integers; its original checker skipped date-time and URI formats); Plans/dch_retained_recipes.json pins their exact original schemas and source revisions. A skipped format check never authenticates invalid history (CV-1101, SP-1101): frozen validators apply the shared date-time predicate and CV-253 to the recipe's pinned original resources, so a retained timestamp CV-1101 refuses is owner-invalid and refuses, while owner-valid lowercase, leap-second and long-fraction history stays readable with its exact spelling; the skipped URI check is preserved. Never re-encode raw-v1 bytes under a later normalization to verify their commitment. Plans/dch_write_recipe_receipts.json is an independent synthetic Storage receipt adapter, not native authentication evidence. Every earlier-valid retained numeric or format record stays readable with current authorization, deletion/hold access, withdrawal and actual-source identity checks. A forged source or recipe selection still refuses. Current derived checkpoints may copy an old event sequence into their exact new integer representation; the original retained event/index sequence and commitment remain unchanged. A retry verifies its saved original through the same historical schema/byte/custody reader before comparison; its incoming input stays strict-v4, and a replay-only compatibility original still cannot authorize a current append or retry. Different earlier semantic values conflict without sending an out-of-current-domain original through the current RFC 8785 encoder. A retained checkpoint, including its history and physical payload pack, uses its own original write provenance separately from its referenced event.

The strict-v4 format validators are mandatory and installed explicitly, never through optional jsonschema plugins. Timestamps adopt the shared CV-1101 check: every current and frozen DCH validator is pm_event_datetime.datetime_validator over the complete outer schema, so the registered RFC 3339 predicate runs through the validator. occurred_at_utc keeps the EventRecord profile (T or t, Z/z or a signed offset, any fraction length, year 0000 and legitimate offset-adjusted leap seconds); observed_at_utc and persisted_at_utc keep CV-253's storage_utc_z profile through the inventory-classified envelope; the family ts and populated checkpoint retired_at_utc take the same predicate with their unchanged owner-schema terminal uppercase-Z pattern. A missing zone, space or wrong separator, invalid calendar field, hour 24, minute 60, false leap second, empty fraction and trailing LF refuse. Timestamp strings are never rewritten and are compared only as exact strings; no DCH-local timestamp grammar remains. PR URLs where declared fully match RFC 3986 HTTPS syntax, including valid percent escapes, reg-name or bracketed IPv6/IPvFuture host, numeric port and path/query/fragment grammar. Malformed brackets/hosts/escapes and whitespace refuse. No PR-host allowlist or new provider behavior is introduced. UUID contexts keep Storage's enforced descriptor. Both payload editions, all three EventRecord timestamps and populated checkpoint retirement times have isolated format negatives; applicable PR payloads cover every malformed URL form.
```

The checkpoint is MessagePack canonical, max 16 KiB under SP-340; oversized values use existing SP-337 reference storage, never an exemption. The closed history array stores at most two full prior checkpoint generations with first retired_at_utc and state retired; current fields name the selected generation. Reserve staged slots through the existing maintenance intent before source staging; a staged candidate counts against three even before it is visible in history. Retain at most three publication generations per exact key under RP-PROJECTION-3GEN@1.0.0; retirement starts at first committed replacement, retries do not reset it, 604800 seconds for eligible retired generations only, with holds/current/staged/live-ref protection. Reserve the slot first or disclose rebuild unavailability. Source events keep PENDING_RETENTION_DECISION; the checkpoint gives no source keepalive. Backup restores canonical source/custody/tombstones first; derived target/checkpoint is rebuilt and validated against the current full-index token before read. Withdrawal fences this projector and its domain readers in addition to the passive reader, sets checkpoint state withdrawn by CAS, and refuses all ordinary advances. Retained historical lookup uses original schema and current access checks; successor publication requires a separately versioned, complete shadow rebuild. Unsupported versions are unavailable, never rewritten in place.

Adopt SP-337 for this exact event body. The logical body remains the selected closed Project/application payload edition, with its existing field and array bounds unchanged. Encode that complete body as SP-236 canonical MessagePack (recursive exact UTF-8 map-key order and shortest encodings); measure encoded bytes, not JSON characters or the envelope. At most 16384 bytes may be inline with payload_ref=null. An oversized inline body is refused before append. Larger or separately governed bodies use payload={} and the newly authored string binding `payload:v1:{lowercase_blake3_64}:{decimal_byte_size}:application/msgpack` in EventRecord.payload_ref, with canonical unsigned decimal size, selecting the existing payload-pack index key `payload:v1:{lowercase_blake3_64}`. The reference commits to the BLAKE3 of the exact complete encoded body, exact byte size and media type application/msgpack. Resolve and decode that original body, validate its exact schema/edition and every scope/identity/actor/time join as for inline bodies; a reference is never an empty semantic body. Require actual original Storage instance, Server/scope/Computer/thread custody, current authorization/deletion/hold access checks, durable exact pack bytes and index entry and verified readback before the referencing append can be acknowledged or its first receipt/result published. Missing, changed, unauthorized, deleted, wrong-store or unreadable body/index evidence refuses publication; no base64 body, truncated body, alternate-source reconstruction or rerun is allowed. Pack durability, reference counts, holds, backups and deletion deadlines remain SP-337; this binding grants no new retention exemption.

Checkpoint acceptance compares original source facts independently of the candidate: the outer storage_instance_id, durable-token storage_instance_id, source_selection storage_instance_id and actual source/root instance must be identical. Resolve the token checkpoint_key in the actual full-index root, its uniquely current generation JSON Pointer checkpoint_ref and exact same-instance event_record_index.v2@generation dataset. Require exact generation anchor, current frontier revision/digest and all source_selection fields against current synchronized source, including nonmatching same-generation appends; a shape-valid stale token cannot publish. The domain checkpoint key binds this instance and exact scope_partition. last_event_id/last_sequence_id join the actual exact-family EventRecord and its full-index row and source-value commitment; actual source Computer/thread/scope also join the published projection. Publication_id, revision, projection_refs and the full durable source token match the actual staged/read-back publication selected by the atomic checkpoint/pointer CAS. Independent source, token, selection, key/ref, event, dataset, publication and current-frontier mismatches refuse publication. Static fixture adapters model these joins; they do not prove native full-index coverage, redb transactions, CRC, source locks or durability.

For chat.thread_deleted, the complete encoded checkpoint includes every retained history entry and projection reference. Measure that entire SP-236 value at the 16384-byte SP-340 boundary: 16384 bytes may be inline, 16385 bytes may not. A larger logical checkpoint keeps the same closed schema and bounds and uses SP-337; measure the stored reference/pointer too. Resolve the exact complete bytes through their BLAKE3/size/media-type reference and same-instance, exact-key/scope/family payload-pack index, with current authorization/deletion/hold access, durable bytes/index and verified readback before checkpoint publication. Externalizing the event body does not externalize this checkpoint. Every Storage-assigned identity and metadata field is checked against the original Storage record for the actual instance; no fixture/default instance supplies authority. Checkpoint source lookup resolves inline or referenced originals, validates the supported original envelope and Project/application payload edition, verifies their exact original source commitment and current access/withdrawal status, and then joins their source facts. Retained compatibility-reader originals, including projector_replay_only, remain readable after later live-state changes; only a new append/retry uses the current-writer policy. Unsupported, withdrawn, forged or foreign originals cannot publish. Newly written integer and boolean slots require their exact types before comparison or arithmetic; string numbers/booleans, null, arrays and nested objects confer no numeric or access authority. Current physical commitment/reference encoding canonicalizes integral numeric aliases and signed zero to the same shortest integer bytes; retained bytes retain their protected original recipe below. These are refinements of this family's existing SP-236/SP-278/SP-337/SP-340 contract, not a new retention or product decision.

Before any source resolution or identity hashing, validate every Storage-instance context against Storage's own UUID descriptor in Plans/event_record_index_checkpoint.schema.json, including exact primitive type and UUID format. Empty, malformed, overlong, newline-suffixed and non-string instances refuse even when dependent IDs, keys and source commitments agree. Compare candidate, token, source-selection, payload-pack and index context against the independently read actual Storage record; a caller context, default instance or coherent forged context supplies no authority. Verify Storage-assigned sequence and timestamp fields against that exact original record commitment before reading. A retained original remains governed by its supported edition and current custody, not later lifecycle state.

For new writes and current identity/idempotency inputs, this family selects strict-v4 exact integer types with the owner-declared domain of each field. Storage sequence_id and its last_sequence_id copies, frontier_revision, selected_segment_generation, manifest_generation, recovery_epoch and pack byte_size retain exact uint64 values 0 through 18446744073709551615; no 2^53 ceiling applies to Storage metadata. Publication revision and logical payload integers retain their existing owner minima and maxima, with no invented DCH safe-integer cap. Declared integer slots reject runtime float/string/bool/null/array/object substitutes except explicitly nullable slots. Storage metadata is excluded from the producer-semantic projection as already specified. The producer route is the CV-1100 qualified RFC 8785 encoding of the unchanged CV-317 producer projection (shared producer_semantic_bytes/producer_semantic_digest); an unsupported exact producer input is a structured route refusal, without narrowing its logical owner domain, rounding or stringification. Physical bytes follow SP-236 through the shared SP-1100 codec (storage_value_bytes, EVENT_VALUE profile): float type, minimal exact float width and signed zero are preserved, so a lexical alias never shares an integer's bytes, and the exact integer slots refuse every alias; invalid JSON 01 refuses under the CV-1100 current parser. Retained-recipe dispatch composes the shared SP-1101 RetainedDispatcher and timestamps use the shared CV-1101 check, as the retained-original and format paragraphs state. Test Storage write/retry inputs at 2^53, 2^60 and uint64 maximum, and refuse overflow, negative and wrong-type metadata independently.

Retained and compatibility originals use the schema, numeric domain, runtime type policy, format validator and physical encoder in force when written. The single selector record_number_rule() owns this dispatch on passive history, SP-337 materialization/reference verification, full-index source/checkpoint validation, checkpoint physical storage, saved-original retry comparison and terminal retained-start lookup. New/current inputs select strict-v4. For retained sources, independently read protected Storage write-receipt provenance binds actual storage_instance_id, exact original source-value SHA-256 and recipe_id; it is committed with the original write and survives restore with that source. Candidate fields, caller version/recipe flags, mutable live state and payload content cannot select or enroll an earlier recipe. Verify any claim against that independently authenticated provenance, then verify the exact original bytes with the selected recipe. Missing earlier provenance is unavailable under that earlier recipe, never a guessed downgrade: an original of a Store outside the sealed write custody refuses as unavailable and a receipt naming a recipe with no installed frozen verifier refuses as unsupported, with no fallback to another recipe; within a custody Store an original without a legacy receipt was written by the current strict-v4 writer. Each retained read composes the shared SP-1101 RetainedDispatcher once: one owner selection, no caller override and no current-then-legacy probing, and the installed frozen verifier of that exact recipe tuple (pinned to the recipe's recorded original schema hashes) checks the original. Preserve raw-v1 (d36809af original MessagePack numeric types), normalized-v2 (a785466d normalized integral floats with the original uncapped integer domain), and strict-v3 (c21fa62e safe integers; its original checker skipped date-time and URI formats); Plans/dch_retained_recipes.json pins their exact original schemas and source revisions. A skipped format check never authenticates invalid history (CV-1101, SP-1101): frozen validators apply the shared date-time predicate and CV-253 to the recipe's pinned original resources, so a retained timestamp CV-1101 refuses is owner-invalid and refuses, while owner-valid lowercase, leap-second and long-fraction history stays readable with its exact spelling; the skipped URI check is preserved. Never re-encode raw-v1 bytes under a later normalization to verify their commitment. Plans/dch_write_recipe_receipts.json is an independent synthetic Storage receipt adapter, not native authentication evidence. Every earlier-valid retained numeric or format record stays readable with current authorization, deletion/hold access, withdrawal and actual-source identity checks. A forged source or recipe selection still refuses. Current derived checkpoints may copy an old event sequence into their exact new integer representation; the original retained event/index sequence and commitment remain unchanged. A retry verifies its saved original through the same historical schema/byte/custody reader before comparison; its incoming input stays strict-v4, and a replay-only compatibility original still cannot authorize a current append or retry. Different earlier semantic values conflict without sending an out-of-current-domain original through the current RFC 8785 encoder. A retained checkpoint, including its history and physical payload pack, uses its own original write provenance separately from its referenced event.

The strict-v4 format validators are mandatory and installed explicitly, never through optional jsonschema plugins. Timestamps adopt the shared CV-1101 check: every current and frozen DCH validator is pm_event_datetime.datetime_validator over the complete outer schema, so the registered RFC 3339 predicate runs through the validator. occurred_at_utc keeps the EventRecord profile (T or t, Z/z or a signed offset, any fraction length, year 0000 and legitimate offset-adjusted leap seconds); observed_at_utc and persisted_at_utc keep CV-253's storage_utc_z profile through the inventory-classified envelope; the family ts and populated checkpoint retired_at_utc take the same predicate with their unchanged owner-schema terminal uppercase-Z pattern. A missing zone, space or wrong separator, invalid calendar field, hour 24, minute 60, false leap second, empty fraction and trailing LF refuse. Timestamp strings are never rewritten and are compared only as exact strings; no DCH-local timestamp grammar remains. PR URLs where declared fully match RFC 3986 HTTPS syntax, including valid percent escapes, reg-name or bracketed IPv6/IPvFuture host, numeric port and path/query/fragment grammar. Malformed brackets/hosts/escapes and whitespace refuse. No PR-host allowlist or new provider behavior is introduced. UUID contexts keep Storage's enforced descriptor. Both payload editions, all three EventRecord timestamps and populated checkpoint retirement times have isolated format negatives; applicable PR payloads cover every malformed URL form.
